title: What Led to Maria Bartiromo’s Downfall at Fox News
partialText: The network this week took Maria Bartiromo off the air, pulling one of the last hosts whose coverage of Dominion Voting Systems drew an expensive defamation lawsuit.

title: Will a Turnaround Plan Revive Volkswagen or Merely Delay Its Demise?
partialText: The beleaguered auto giant reached a deal with unions to cut tens of thousands of jobs and slash production. Is it enough to revive an iconic German company?

title: Authors Wrangle With Publishers Over $1.5 Billion Anthropic A.I. Settlement
partialText: The tech giant must pay $3,000 per pirated book that it used to train its chatbot. Many authors fear they could lose funds to others in the book business.

title: Kenyans Made a Living Writing College Essays. Then A.I. Arrived.
partialText: Thousands of Kenyans made a living writing essays for overseas students. With A.I., the work has dried up, a warning for online gig work that has been a global lifeline.

title: California Forever’s Ambitious Plan Faces Another Setback
partialText: A legislative setback for a manufacturing and housing proposal shows how hard it remains to build in the largest state — and why a backlash against billionaires could make it even harder.

title: The Heart Drug Pelacarsen Fails, Shocking Novartis and Cardiologists
partialText: Doctors were hopeful the drug, which was being tested in a large clinical trial by Novartis, was going to be a powerful new tool to fight heart disease.

title: What to know about the report.

partialText: The president said he could halt trade between the United States and countries with which it has a trade deficit if the central bank doesn’t do his bidding.

title: The U.S. Wants the Oil From These 17 Venezuelan Fields
partialText: A private oil company has struck a deal with the Trump administration to develop 17 areas in Venezuela, an effort that experts say will take years and billions of dollars.

title: How Gloria Steinem and Ms. Magazine Transformed the Publishing Industry
partialText: The feminist icon insisted that women were not a niche audience — and proved it in 1971 with the start of an influential publication owned and operated by them.

title: Tesla’s Cybercab Is Being Investigated by Federal Regulators
partialText: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said it would examine whether the company’s new self-driving taxi, which has no steering wheel, meets federal auto regulations.

title: The Pros and Cons of Paying Off Your Mortgage Early
partialText: Homeowners who make extra payments can save thousands of dollars in interest. But, financial experts say, paying down other debt, with higher interest rates, may be a better option.

title: Robust Hiring Reinforces Strength of the U.S. Economy
partialText: Employers added 162,000 jobs and unemployment held at 4.1 percent last month, signs of a stability that contrasted with high inflation weighing on households and markets.

title: The job market in 2035: More nurses, fewer secretaries.

partialText: Around the world, rising bond yields reflect shifting expectations on how fast policymakers will raise interest rates.

title: Notre Dame’s Jersey Patch Deal With SoFi Divides Alumni and Fans
partialText: Alumni have varying opinions about the school’s deal with the personal finance company SoFi to advertise on Notre Dame athletic uniforms.

title: Wineries Are Offering Bingo, Picnics, Jewelry … and Sometimes Wine
partialText: With slumping sales and fewer tourists, California winemakers have turned to special events and classes to woo customers — even those who don’t drink.

title: Iran War Helps to Drive U.S. Diesel Prices to New High
partialText: Because of the war in Iran, the cost has exceeded the record it hit in 2022 after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

title: Former Labor Secretary Stoked Dysfunction and Toxicity, Department Report Finds
partialText: Lori Chavez-DeRemer spent Labor Department funds on personal travel and tolerated harassment in the agency, its inspector general found.

partialText: The network sued the agency last month to stop it from taking steps that could force ABC stations off the air. The F.C.C. said the lawsuit was premature.

partialText: The new Cybercab embodies Elon Musk’s vision of cars that drive themselves, but it is not clear when the vehicle will be widely available.

title: Volkswagen Plans to Cut 50,000 Jobs
partialText: Facing growing competition from China and rapidly advancing technology, the German auto giant said its board had approved a “comprehensive” overhaul.

partialText: Higher costs for home loans have put a squeeze on the housing market, adding pressure to consumers already struggling with elevated inflation.

partialText: The dismissal came after Ms. Bartiromo shared internal Fox Business communications with the White House, a person familiar with the details confirmed.

title: Bessent Blames Ukraine for High Energy Prices
partialText: After meeting with Russia’s finance minister, the Treasury secretary said Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure were contributing to a global energy shock driven mainly by the U.S. war with Iran.

title: Leon Black Sues Congressional Panel Investigating Epstein
partialText: The billionaire skipped a deposition on Thursday and filed a lawsuit seeking to block a House committee’s subpoenas demanding nondisclosure agreements he may have made with women.

title: The Athletic Says Dianna Russini’s Relationship With Mike Vrabel Violated Its Standards
partialText: The New York Times-owned publication said the relationship between its former reporter Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel of the Patriots gave the appearance of a conflict of interest.

title: Schools Giving Aid to Minority Students Could Lose Tax Exemptions Under Trump’s New Rules
partialText: The Treasury Department released rules that would prevent schools with race-based programs from qualifying for tax-exempt status, a threat to both higher education and other private schools.

title: U.S. Trade Gap Ballooned in July
partialText: The trade deficit bounced back up last month as spending on data centers to feed the A.I. boom drove up imports.

title: Rate Rise in Play as Fed Officials Await Inflation Data

partialText: The acquisition of the start-up is an indication of Nvidia’s growing role as Silicon Valley’s central banker and its emphasis on open-source technology.

partialText: This week’s renewed strikes by the United States and Iran strain the flow of energy and diminish expectations the disruption will end soon.

partialText: In addition, the F.C.C. is weighing stiff restrictions on common drone technology such as thermal imaging and aerosol spraying.

partialText: The airline said that lounges in Baltimore, Honolulu, Nashville and Austin, Texas, would debut starting late next year, and that seven more were in the works.

partialText: The Agriculture Department offered new initiatives for ranchers after President Trump said he would import more beef. The moves aren’t a quick fix.

title: Global Bond Rates Are Rising. What Should You Do Now?
partialText: If you own bonds, they may be in a broad fund that hasn’t lost much money. And that fund may do much better in the next several years.

title: FiveThirtyEight’s Podcast Hosts Reunite for a New Show

title: Saturday Evening Post Will Stop Printing After 205 Years
partialText: The magazine, famous for publishing Jack London stories and Norman Rockwell art, will continue online.

partialText: In times of natural disasters and other dangers, special features tucked away on your iPhone or Android device could help make a difference.

title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
partialText: Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.

title: What to Know About Venezuelan Energy Following Trump’s Oil Deal
